text.description: The words said. Variables go in braces ({first}); the engine fills them. Said exactly as written unless the line is generated, and then the fallback and the meaning a generated wording is held to.

interruptible.description: Whether the caller may talk over the line (barge-in). false for lines that must be heard whole, such as a keypad instruction or a legal statement.

mode.description: How the line is produced. fixed: the text above, word for word. generative: worded by a model for the moment (it needs a `goal`), under checks that hold it to this line's data and meaning, with the text above said whenever a check fails or the model is slow. Absent: fixed, unless its form says `wording: generative`; `mode: fixed` keeps a line of such a form fixed.

goal.description: What a generated line must do, for the model that words it ("Ask when the outage started; briefly acknowledge what they just said."). Required with mode: generative. In a locale's prompts.yaml: the line is generated in that locale only where its goal is given there.

prescribed.description: true: the line is prescribed (regulated, legal or otherwise fixed by the app designer) and is always said word for word: never generated, whatever its form says; `pnpm check` refuses mode: generative on it. The policy card lists it.

situations.description: The situations the line is generated in; in any other it is said word for word. first-ask: the line has not been said before on this call; re-ask: it has (asked again after a miss, a no or a change); after-correction: this turn the caller changed a value they had given, or said no to a read-back; frustrated: the caller has been frustrated on this call. Absent: every situation.

channels.description: The channels the line is generated on (voice: a call; chat: a web chat); on another it is said word for word. Absent: both.

when.description: Where a generated line is generated; everywhere else its fixed text is said. Both parts must hold.

acknowledge.description: Whether the generated wording of this line may begin by acknowledging what the caller just said ("Thanks.", "Got it."). false: the model only rewords the fixed line, and is told so. Default true; a line's own setting wins over its form's (forms.yaml's `acknowledge`). Only with a generated line; never on a framed line (a span acknowledges nothing).

from.description: Generated from collected content: the line's variables (its {names}) that hold content the call collected (a message, a note) and the model may summarize rather than repeat word for word. The exact content is always kept and is what is stored; the fixed text, which reads it word for word, is the fallback, and a caller who asks to hear it again hears it. Only with a generated line.

summarizesConfirmed.description: true: the app accepts that this generated line, a read-back, may summarize a value named in `from` (or in a span's `from`) that a `confirmed` rule holds the caller to (the caller confirms the value kept, word for word, after hearing a summary of it). Required for such a line; the policy card says so on the action.

generate.description: A fixed line with generated spans (the framed form): each key is one of the line's {variables}, worded by a model from the content its `from` names; every other word of the line is the app's fixed text, never sent to a model and never changed. The frame says whose words the span gives ("{caller} called and left this message: {summary}"), so attribution is by design. A span that is not generated, or fails a check, is the exact content, word for word. Not with `mode` or a line's own `goal` or `from`.

from.description: The slot whose content the span is worded from (the message, the note): the caller's words, collected. The model is sent only this content, quoted, with the span's goal; the exact content is what is stored, and it fills the span word for word whenever the span is not generated or a check fails. Required in prompts.yaml; a locale gives a span only its goal.

goal.description: What the span must say, for the model that words it ("Summarize the caller's message in one sentence, in their own terms."). In a locale's prompts.yaml: the span is generated in that locale only where its goal is given there.

words.description: The most words the span may use; a longer one is not said (the exact content is). Default 25.

speaks.description: Whose person the span speaks in. as-caller (the default): in the caller's own terms, as they said it ("call me back"), under a frame that gives their words ("{caller} left this message: {summary}"). to-caller: to the caller, about their own message, as a receptionist reads one back: their I, me, my, we and our said as you and your ("call you back"), and a name the line says ({recipient}, {caller}) put in place of a pronoun only where the message makes clear who is meant; under a frame that speaks to them ("{recipient} gets your message, in short: {summary}"), never one that says they "said" it. English only for now: in another language the span is worded as-caller. Read from prompts.yaml, for every locale.

additionalProperties.description: One generated span of a fixed line.

exactText.description: A framed line only (`generate`): the frame said when every span is its exact content, word for word (no model set up, a check that fails, a slow model, a read-back after a no, a repeat, a reading `when` leaves fixed); `text` is then the frame said with a generated span. For a frame whose words are true of a summary only ("called and said, in short, {summary}"), the exact words get a frame of their own ("called and said: {summary}"). It names the same variables as `text`. Absent: `text` is said either way. In a locale's prompts.yaml: that locale's own, needed there where prompts.yaml gives one.

description: prompts.yaml: the lines the agent says, for one locale.
